beliefs: f reverses the order of characters in the string [E1]
f then swaps the case of each letter (upper<->lower), leaving non-letters unchanged [E1, E3]
The case swap is applied to the reversed string, not the original [E3]
The first output character is the case-swapped last input character shifted back by 2 alphabetically within its own case (a->y, A->Y, wrapping z->x, Z->X) [E4, E5, E6, E11]
Non-ASCII letters are treated as letters: they are case-swapped (é->É) and shifted back by 2 within the Latin-1 letter range (é->ç, ñ->ï, ü->ú) [E12]
The -2 shift applies only when the last character is a letter; otherwise the first output char is just the reversed last char [E8, E9]
notes: E12 shows non-ASCII letters are shifted by -2 within their own alphabet block (é->ç, ñ->ï, ü->ú) rather than being treated as non-letters; updated transform to shift any isalpha char by -2 within its case block using Unicode-aware case detection, falling back to codepoint arithmetic for non-ASCII.
